key_insight: A partially-averaged Navier-Stokes (PANS) model can capture curvature-driven turbulence effects in annular Poiseuille flow with accuracy comparable to DNS and other scale-resolving RANS-based methods.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a lower-cost alternative for predicting turbulent flow in annular geometries relevant to heat exchangers and similar industrial systems.
method: Simulated turbulent annular Poiseuille flow at Re_Dh = 8900.
Used the PANS variable-resolution turbulence model built on a RANS framework.
Examined the influence of inner-to-outer radius ratio (η = Ri/Ro) on the flowfield and anisotropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the PANS results capture the effects of transverse wall curvature comparably to DNS and other scale-resolving RANS-based approaches.
watch_item: Performance is reported for a specific Reynolds number and geometry range, so broader generalization and model tuning for other annular-flow conditions may still be needed.
paper_title: Partially-Averaged Navier-Stokes simulation of turbulent annular Poiseulle flow
